text:
sam: Heads-up — console wants richer route attribution for the per-route table. Proposal: switch SDKs to emit X-Route-Meta v2 as base64(json) (so we can add priority/quota/tags without exploding header parsing). Need input on ops/SDK break risk and sampling behavior.

joel: base64-json makes sense for flexibility, but proxies/NGINX have header size limits. What's the expected payload?

sam: Typical payload would be tiny, e.g. `{"version":2,"policy":"weighted","priority":"gold","quota":"alpha"}` then base64. Usually <200 bytes.

nina: Also: some customers run older edge proxies that strip unusual headers or drop long ones. We need a fallback plain header (short key=value) for compatibility.

liam: Can we do both? SDKs send short X-Route (v1) and X-Route-Meta v2 (base64) when opt-in true. Console prefers v2, falls back to v1. That keeps old clients safe.

joel: Agree. From SDK implementation POV: add opt-in flag default=false. Example TS: `new Redwood({ key, routeMetaOptIn: true, routeMeta: {priority: 'gold', quota: 'alpha', tags: ['ui','realtime']} })`. We'll emit both headers when opt-in=true.

alex: Important: telemetry. We must mark rows that came from sampled v2 payloads vs v1 derived. Add `meta_source` field in analytics events.

sam: Good. Also propose a sampling hint: `X-Route-Meta-Sample: 0.01` when customer wants to reduce traffic. SDKs should not sample higher than org-level quota without explicit consent.

nina: For Python SDK, we should expose an async callback to compute routeMeta per-request instead of static constructor-only field. Some apps set dynamic priority based on user or prompt.

joel: Note for Go: we should avoid allocating JSON per token path. Provide helper that encodes only if changed. We'll add a small LRU cache keyed by the routeMeta map. Implementation detail but reduces perf impact.

liam: On console UX — show an info-pill on sampled rows and a toggle to "Show raw route-meta" (humanized). Also add a warning if many rows are coming from v1 fallback.

sam: Rollout plan I suggest:
1) SDKs: add v2 emit behind opt-in flag + sampling header support + per-request hook (python).
2) Server: accept both headers, decode v2 base64 safely, enforce max header size and strip if too big. Log decode failures to `route-meta-decodes` counter.
3) Console: staging-only tile reads v2, shows banner "beta route meta" and sampled badge.
4) Canary orgs opt-in (internal + 2 customers).
5) Monitor telemetry: `meta_source`, `decode_errors`, per-org sample rate.
6) Gradual opt-in rollout and GA.

alex: That plan sounds safe. Action items: joel to make SDK PRs (ts/go/py) with opt-in=false default; nina to add server decode + metrics; liam to add console UI banner + sampled badge; sam to coordinate canary customers and messaging.

joel: Tests: roundtrip test for base64 encode/decode, smoke test where console falls back to v1 if v2 invalid, header size regression test. I'll add unit + e2e.

nina: Ops concern: proxies that sanitize headers may drop base64 header. We'll include a short v1 header so attribution isn't lost. Also add a server-side aggregator that reconstructs v2 from v1 when possible and marks as `reconstructed_from_v1`.

sam: Messaging: customer-facing note should emphasize opt-in, sampling, and no forced change, and provide upgrade snippets for each SDK.

joel: I'll prepare example snippets:
TS:
```
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.KEY, routeMetaOptIn: true, routeMetaSampler: 0.02 });
client.setRouteMeta(() => ({ priority: 'gold', quota: 'alpha' }));
```
Python:
```
client = Redwood(key=os.getenv('KEY'), route_meta_opt_in=True, route_meta_sampler=0.02)
@client.route_meta_hook
async def meta(req):
    return { 'priority': 'gold', 'quota': 'alpha' }
```
Go:
```
c := redwood.NewClient(opts.WithKey(os.Getenv("KEY")), opts.WithRouteMetaOptIn(false))
// provide per-request meta via context value
```

liam: Where will the docs live? Need a doc page with header examples + proxy guidance.

sam: I'll draft docs in the internal docs repo and link in the PRs. Also include a troubleshooting section (decode errors, size issues).

deploy-bot: deploy: console canary to staging-console-5 started — 3 nodes. Link: https://deploys.redwood/staging/console/5

ci-bot: CI: joel/sdk-ts#234 added new tests — all green on ubuntu-latest.

alex: Follow-up sync tomorrow 9:30am. If decode_errors spike we rollback console tile.

liam: 👍 I'll mock a customer proxy that strips headers to validate fallback behavior.

sam: Thanks everyone. Tagging @here so product/ops know this is opt-in only for now.
